messages:
Alex: quick follow-up from the RFC review — we need to lock down the service auth boundary tradeoffs before we list migration steps. TL;DR: do we allow project-scoped API keys to be accepted directly by internal services, or must they always be proxied/translated by an operator component? :thinking:
Mira: my vote is proxy-only. project keys are user-facing and have weaker guards. letting internal services accept them expands blast radius.
Devin: agree on blast radius, but proxy adds latency and complexity. can we do a hybrid: accept project keys for read-only endpoints, require operator-issued tokens for write/exec?
Alex: good point. hybrid could help adoption. need clear rules though, otherwise every service will implement slightly different checks.
Sam: what about token introspection / short TTLs? operator can mint ephemeral tokens for services with a 1m TTL to limit risk, plus traceability.
Mira: operator-issued short-lived tokens + audience claim seems ideal. services validate aud and issuer. rejects raw project keys.
Devin: operational cost: we need a fast/locally-cached introspection path so we don't call central auth on every request. suggest local JWK cache + revocation stream via pubsub.
Alex: agreed. design points to capture: 1) operator mints tokens with `iss=redwood-operator` and `aud=service:<name>`, 2) services accept operator tokens only, 3) project keys usable only at edge/proxy, 4) revocation via pubsub + local cache.
Mira: small auth header example for operator token:
```
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...
X-Redwood-Aud: service:ingest
```
Devin: for backward compat we should provide a migration shim: proxy translates project key -> operator token and signs it, adds `x-forwarded-for-key-id` header. services can log that header to track origin during migration.
Sam: +1. timeline: enable proxy-translation, rollout operator token validation in services (95% read-only endpoints first), flip default deny for write endpoints.
Alex: security checklist: add audit log entries for every translation, enforce token TTL <= 2m for translated tokens, add metrics: translation_rate, token_rejects_by_aud.
sec-bot: automated note: please file follow-up RFC issues — tag `authn/authz` and include migration checklist template.
Mira: open Q: how do we treat third-party integrations (partner API keys)? treat as project keys and force proxy, or create distinct partner token flow?
Devin: recommend partner tokens as separate contract — operator issues partner tokens with `scope=partner` and distinct audience. avoids confusing metrics and RBAC rules.
Alex: action items: (1) Mira to draft operator token spec (iss/aud/ttl/claims) by EOD Tue, (2) Devin to prototype JWK cache + revocation stream next week, (3) Sam to stub proxy-translation headers and logging. I'll collect these into the follow-up RFC.
Sam: noted. I'll also add a small perf test for translation latency (goal <5ms p50).
Mira: thanks — will also add examples for `rbac` claim shape for service-level checks.
Alex: cool. if no objections I'll create the RFC follow-up and link here. :lock:
